data.title: Halfords Earnings Call Shows Strong Growth Despite Caution
data.description:
Halfords Group plc ((GB:HFD)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Halfords delivered a strongly positive first-half performance, with gains in sales, margins, profit, cash generation and returns. Management raised full-year profit guidance and the interim dividend, although it cautioned that unusually warm weather will not recur, second-half margins may moderate and Avayler remains loss-making.

Strong First-Half Group Performance

Halfords increased like-for-like sales by 7.1%, while underlying operating margin rose 140 basis points to 4.6%. Underlying profit before tax jumped 66% to £39 million, and return on capital improved 530 basis points to 18.9%.

Underlying Growth Excluding Weather

After removing an estimated £8 million benefit from exceptionally warm weather, like-for-like sales still grew 5.6%. Underlying operating margin increased to 3.8%, profit before tax rose 31.9% to £31 million and return on capital remained comfortably above the cost of capital at 16.9%.

Revenue and Gross-Margin Expansion

Revenue climbed 6.7% to £953 million, while gross margin widened 120 basis points to 52.6%. Halfords attributed the improvement to effective pricing, promotional activity, favourable foreign exchange and a stronger mix of seasonal categories.

Operating Leverage Improves Profitability

Operating costs rose 6.2%, below the rate of revenue growth, showing the benefit of cost discipline and operating leverage. This was achieved despite wage and fuel inflation, higher incentive provisions and continued investment, helping underlying profit before tax rise from £23.5 million to £39 million.

Retail Sales and Profit Growth

Retail revenue increased 7.3% to £572 million, with like-for-like sales up 7.7%. Motoring grew 7.3% and cycling 8.3%, while retail operating profit rose 46.1% to £30.1 million and the margin improved from 3.9% to 5.3%.

Category Management Shows Early Gains

Wave One category-management trials covered about 15% of retail sales and included workshops, flagship cycling and cycling parts and accessories. The trialled categories delivered more than 5% growth in both sales and margin, supporting Halfords’ plan to relaunch about 60% of its ranges by the end of FY28.

Cycling and E-Bike Momentum

Cycling sales grew by more than 8%, with bikes and parts and accessories contributing broadly similar growth. Electric-bike sales rose 45% year on year, and e-bikes accounted for about one-quarter of all bikes sold.

Autocentres Growth and Margin Improvement

Excluding Avayler, Autocentres revenue rose 5.9% to £380.2 million, with like-for-like sales growth of 6.1%. Underlying operating profit increased by more than 60% to £16.1 million, lifting the operating margin from 2.8% to 4.2%.

Autocentres Productivity Advances

Autocentres reduced labour costs as a share of sales by more than 200 basis points, helped by improved garage utilisation. Additional work identified represented about one-quarter of consumer-garage revenue, while tyre market share and income per tyre also benefited from services such as wheel alignment and warranties.

Fusion Program Supports Garage Expansion

There were 121 Fusion sites trading, and the rollout remained on track for completion by the end of the financial year. The format typically pays back within two years, giving management confidence that the garages business can progress towards its medium-term 5% to 6% operating-margin goal.

Digital and Retail Services Develop

Group online sales grew by just under 6%, with 80% of online orders collected in stores. Services grew faster than product sales, supported by higher profit per job and particularly strong demand for bike servicing, repairs and dash-cam fitting.

Strong Cash Generation and Balance Sheet

Halfords generated £38 million of free cash flow and ended the period with net cash of £40.1 million. Including lease liabilities, net debt fell to £207 million from £228.7 million at the FY26 year-end, while the £180 million revolving credit facility remained undrawn.

Distribution Center Investment

Halfords has signed a lease for a new distribution center in Coventry, scheduled to open in FY30. The company plans to fund £40 million to £50 million of capital investment directly over the next three years, while £35 million to £45 million of related non-underlying operating costs will remain within existing guardrails.

Distribution Center Expected to Add Value

Management expects the new center to deliver low- to mid-teens millions of pounds in annual profit benefits once mature. Benefits are expected to begin in FY30 and build through FY32, while the project should improve customer service and colleague experience and generate returns well above the cost of capital.

Interim Dividend Increased

The Board declared an interim dividend of 3.5 pence per share, up from 3 pence in the comparable period. Halfords’ policy is to cover dividends by between 1.5 and 2.5 times profit after tax.

Investment in Brand and Capability

Halfords has begun investing in a new brand platform and is increasing spending on marketing, technology, data and colleague capability. Management said the additional investment is intended to support current momentum while strengthening the foundations for longer-term growth.

Resilient Footprint and B2B Revenue

All 366 retail stores were described as profitable, with no store-closure program planned, while the group operates just under 500 garages. About 30% of group revenue comes from business customers, including reliable and recurring fleet-service and MOT work.

Weather Benefit Will Not Be Repeated

Management estimated that the early, warm summer added around £8 million to underlying profit. It stressed that the same favourable weather and incremental earnings cannot be assumed in future periods, making the adjusted performance a more useful guide to underlying momentum.

Second-Half Margin Moderation Expected

First-half margins did not fully reflect the effect of higher oil prices, and Halfords expects margin growth to moderate in the second half. Retail also assumes no further improvement in the gross-margin rate after significant expansion during the past two years.

Inflation and Incentive Costs Rise

The group continues to face wage and fuel inflation, alongside substantially higher incentive costs. Strong first-half results increased the annual bonus provision, while the higher share price raised costs linked to long-term incentive awards.

Avayler Losses Remain a Concern

Avayler revenue was broadly stable, but its operating loss widened to £2.3 million as Halfords continued investing in the platform. External-customer revenue has taken longer to develop than expected, and management is reviewing the business during the second half.

Sales Growth Returns to Normal

Sales growth returned to more typical levels in October and November rather than matching the exceptional pace seen during the hot summer. Halfords also plans to reinvest part of the first-half outperformance into the second half.

Consumer and Market Volatility

Management highlighted risks from a more inflationary environment, sustained high oil prices and potentially higher energy costs. It also warned that weather, consumer confidence and wider industry conditions could create periods of volatility.

Retail Margin Progress May Be Uneven

Management cautioned that progress towards higher retail operating margins should not be expected to move in a straight line. The business must absorb further inflation while continuing to invest in its customer proposition and future growth.

Guidance and Outlook

Halfords raised FY27 underlying profit-before-tax guidance to £60 million-£65 million and expects performance to be weighted towards the first half. It expects second-half margin growth to moderate, targets medium-term operating margins of 5% to 6% in retail and garages, and plans the Coventry center for FY30, with mature annual benefits in the low to mid-teens of millions by FY32.

Halfords’ call combined strong operational delivery with a more measured outlook for the rest of the year. The raised guidance, dividend increase, robust balance sheet and investment pipeline are encouraging, but investors will watch weather normalization, cost pressures, margin progression and the outcome of the Avayler review.

data.title: Finvolution Group Earnings Call Shows Overseas Strength, China Strain
data.description:
Finvolution Group ((FINV)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Finvolution Group’s earnings call delivered a mixed message for investors. Overseas expansion, stronger profitability, liquidity and cost controls offered support, but a sharp China slowdown, weaker asset quality, higher funding costs and lower profit kept management cautious about the pace of recovery.

Revenue Growth Came From Overseas Diversification

Third-quarter revenue rose 11% year over year and 2% sequentially to RMB 949 million. Overseas operations contributed 37% of group revenue, helping offset weakness in the company’s domestic business.

Overseas Volume and Profitability Improved

Overseas loan volume increased 11% year over year to RMB 4 billion and rose 5% from the previous quarter. Overseas operating profit reached RMB 62 million, up 15% sequentially and more than double the year-earlier figure.

International Revenue Mix Passed Its Annual Target

Overseas revenue represented about 31% of total revenue during the first nine months, compared with approximately 20% in 2024 and 25% in 2025. That exceeded the company’s 30% annual target and supports its longer-term ambition to generate more than half of revenue internationally.

Overseas EBITDA Plan Remained on Track

Overseas operating profit totaled approximately RMB 161 million in the first nine months. All three overseas markets were profitable at the operating level and contributed USD 24 million, keeping the business on track for its full-year EBITDA objective.

Overseas Borrower Acquisition Accelerated

Finvolution added 2.8 million new overseas borrowers in the third quarter, a 28% increase from the previous quarter. The figure highlights the company’s continued ability to expand its international customer base despite challenging economic conditions.

Indonesia Expanded Offline Buy Now, Pay Later

Offline Buy Now, Pay Later accounted for about 31% of Indonesia’s third-quarter volume, up from 25% in the prior quarter and 10% a year earlier. Management said the point-of-sale model improves verification of fund use and relies more on merchant networks than paid traffic.

Australia Delivered Stronger Growth and Customer Quality

Australia’s volume rose 21% sequentially, while middle- and large-loan customers reached about half of the portfolio. Deeper open-banking integration and verified data on income, spending and existing debt supported the shift toward higher-quality borrowers.

Fundo Integration Strengthened Australia

Since the Fundo acquisition, Australian new borrowers more than doubled year over year in the third quarter, transaction volume increased nearly 80%, and loan balances doubled. Revenue rose about 50%, while profitability also improved substantially.

Australia Added Digital and Product Capacity

Medium- and large-sized loans represented 51% of Australia’s third-quarter mix, compared with 38% a year earlier. Finvolution’s own app generated 40% of originations, Fundo team retention was about 90%, and management highlighted continued work on products, digital experience and customer retention.

Philippines Credit Performance Beat Expectations

Philippines volume declined 5% sequentially as the business adjusted to a new rate cap, but credit performance was better than expected. Conservative underwriting over the past three quarters helped limit pressure, and management said the transition was largely complete.

China Funding Supply Began to Stabilize

China’s funding supply recovered steadily from its July low through August and September, then remained stable in October and November. Management said available funding had reached a level sufficient for the company’s current risk appetite and origination plan.

Compliance Work Supported Bank Relationships

The company worked with banks on compliant loan products and referral flows, while adding closed-loop payment controls and further checks. It also submitted clean independent audits of fund flows to China’s National Internet Finance Association, helping it remain credible as lenders became more selective.

AI Expanded Collection and Service Capacity

AI collection agents helped replace some capacity lost during an industry-wide campaign targeting collection agencies. Finvolution’s AI applications, including a customer-service agent built on its RAG Fin model, were recognized as exemplary Shanghai cases and have served more than 100 million users.

AI Improved Recovery Rates

For accounts overdue for longer periods, monthly recovery using AI was nearly 1.5 times the rate achieved by third-party collection agencies through phone calls. The result points to potential efficiency gains as the company manages credit losses and customer service at scale.

Liquidity Stayed Strong and Leverage Fell

Cash and short-term investments totaled RMB 8.4 billion at the end of the third quarter, or about USD 1.2 billion. The risk-bearing loan balance divided by shareholders’ equity was 1.5 times, which management described as a historical low.

Share Buybacks and Debt Reduction Continued

Finvolution repurchased USD 4.3 million of shares in the third quarter and USD 71.1 million in the first nine months, reducing shares outstanding by 5.8% from year-end. It also bought back about USD 19 million of convertible senior notes in October, lowering debt and potential dilution.

Operating Expenses Declined Sharply

Group operating expenses fell 27% sequentially to RMB 1.048 billion. Lower sales and marketing costs were the main driver, as the company served more repeat customers through its own app instead of relying as heavily on paid traffic.

Currency Exposure Was Partly Hedged

Management said local-currency assets are matched with local-currency liabilities in overseas markets. This structure is intended to limit the effect of currency movements on the group’s reported results.

China Credit Shock Disrupted Operations

A credit event at another platform in July weakened confidence across China’s loan-facilitation industry. A nationwide campaign against collection agencies that began in late July also reduced collection capacity and efficiency, affecting funding, credit performance and origination.

Group Loan Volume Fell 56%

Group loan volume dropped to approximately RMB 20 billion in the third quarter, down 56% sequentially. The decline was driven mainly by the severe slowdown in China, which outweighed growth in international markets.

China Loan Volume Contracted 61%

China loan volume fell to roughly RMB 16 billion, a 61% sequential decline. Tighter funding supply and elevated credit risk across the industry forced the company to reduce origination significantly.

China Revenue and Take Rate Declined

China revenue fell 38% sequentially to RMB 1.5 billion as the loan book shrank. The take rate declined 30 basis points to about 2.9%, reflecting higher credit and funding costs.

China Asset Quality Weakened

China’s day-one delinquency rate rose to 6.35% from 5.26% in the second quarter, while the 30-day collection rate fell to 85.5% from 89.4%. The CM2 flow rate increased to 0.92% from 0.56%, and the third-quarter vintage cost estimate climbed to 3.5%.

Legacy Loans Continued to Lift Credit Costs

Management expects older loans to remain a source of credit-cost pressure. Total provision expense was broadly flat at RMB 1.35 billion despite lower origination, because credit costs on legacy loans increased.

China Funding Costs Rose Further

China funding costs increased to about 4.3% in the third quarter from approximately 3.7% in the second quarter. Management indicated that costs would remain elevated in the fourth quarter and could move slightly above the third-quarter level.

China Volume Recovery Remained Uncertain

China transaction volume was down about 60% quarter over quarter, and management said funding had not returned to normal. Future volume will depend on loan quality and expected returns, with tight underwriting maintained for new borrowers.

Credit Risk Had Not Reached a Clear Turning Point

The CM2 flow rate fell 6% in October from September as the 30-day collection rate improved modestly. Management cautioned that the change was recent and that, because average loan tenure is eight to nine months, it can take two to three quarters for existing-book risk to work through the portfolio.

Domestic Net Profit Fell 52%

Group net revenue declined 25% sequentially to RMB 2.6 billion, while net profit fell 52% to RMB 206 million. The results reflected lower China origination, higher funding costs and rising credit pressure.

Philippines Volume Fell During the Rate-Cap Shift

Loan volume in the Philippines decreased 5% from the previous quarter as the business adapted to the new rate cap. Management said the adjustment period was largely complete, creating a basis for a measured return to growth.

Macroeconomic Pressure Covered All Overseas Markets

Management cited higher oil prices, inflation and tighter monetary policy across the region. Indonesia faced currency pressure and weaker consumer confidence, the Philippines saw inflation reach 7.2% in September, and Australia’s rate increases put additional pressure on household budgets.

Regulation and Geopolitics Remained Risks

Developing-market regulations can change quickly, and rate-cap changes may slow growth in the short term. Management also highlighted inflation, currency and geopolitical risks in Indonesia and the Philippines, requiring careful monitoring and flexible operating plans.

Guidance Pointed to a Cautious Near-Term Outlook

Finvolution reiterated full-year revenue guidance of RMB 11.5 billion to RMB 12.9 billion but expects to finish near the lower end of the range. Funding costs may remain slightly above third-quarter levels, while China volume recovery will depend on loan quality and returns; overseas EBITDA remains on track for about USD 30 million, with measured Philippines growth and continued Australia investment expected.

The earnings call showed a company with a growing and increasingly profitable international platform, strong liquidity and disciplined spending. Those positives were overshadowed by China’s sharp volume contraction and unresolved credit and funding issues, leaving the recovery story dependent on better asset quality and a gradual improvement in domestic conditions.

data.title: Nanoco Group Earnings Call Signals Progress Amid Risks
data.description:
Nanoco Group plc ((GB:NANO)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Nanoco Group’s earnings call carried a cautiously positive tone. Management highlighted a $5 million LG settlement, lower costs, a £6.2 million opening order book and progress with Asian customers, but the company remains loss-making, cash-burning and exposed to uncertain adoption, timing, customer concentration and technology risks.

Asian Customer Moves Toward Scale-Up

Nanoco has started a three-year joint development agreement with its first Asian chemical customer, which commits to minimum spending of about £0.5 million annually. The program is entering scale-up, with higher material demand expected over the next six months and testing now covering stability and heat stress.

Second Asian Development Agreement Completed

A one-year agreement with a second Asian chemical customer has been completed, also involving indium arsenide materials. Nanoco remains in discussions about a further agreement or additional material purchases, although customer confidentiality limits detail on end markets and supply chains.

Grant Targets and Lead Sulfide Research

Nanoco completed its Innovate UK grant on first-generation lead sulfide and met all project targets. It is continuing work on an internally developed one-step lead sulfide process, supporting its broader effort to improve quantum-dot materials.

LG Settlement Strengthens Intellectual Property Position

The company reached a $5 million settlement with LG Electronics and granted LG a license for display applications. Nanoco also settled with Shoei Chemical, including a covenant not to sue covering key areas of its intellectual property focus.

Product Sales Remain Small but Improved

Product sales were only £13,000 in FY2026, but had reached about £41,000 in FY2027 at the time of the presentation. Management attributed the improvement to business-development investment and continued work on quantum dots and materials that could improve existing technologies.

Lean Operating Structure Cuts Costs

Nanoco reduced its Board from seven members to three and cut headcount from 29 to 23, while retaining core research staff, who now represent more than half of employees. Premises were consolidated without disrupting research or indium arsenide scale-up, reducing cash costs by about £0.3 million a year.

Settlement Drives Better Financial Results

Revenue rose by £3.4 million year on year, largely because of the LG settlement, while adjusted EBITDA increased to £5.3 million from £0.8 million. The improvement reflected settlement income and incremental cost savings rather than a major increase in product sales.

Operating Loss Narrows

Normal operating costs, including cost of sales, research and development and administration, fell from £6.2 million to £5.2 million. The operating loss narrowed to £1.0 million from £2.3 million, while the loss after tax improved to £2.0 million from £2.8 million.

Opening Order Book Provides Visibility

Nanoco entered FY2027 with an opening order book of £6.2 million. This included £5.6 million linked to the release of the Samsung license and £0.6 million from joint development and material orders that had already been invoiced.

Two-Year Cash Runway

Gross cash costs remain broadly stable at £0.3 million to £0.4 million per month. Management said the company would have around two years of runway even with no cash revenue, supported by a low breakeven point and considerable operating leverage.

Investment Continues in Devices and IP

Nanoco plans to spend about £0.1 million on device capabilities and a further £0.1 million on intellectual property during the year. It also intends to test materials on silicon coupons and CMOS integration, with the goal of developing its own Level 3 sensor prototype in FY2027.

Shareholders Back Commercialization

In a shareholder consultation, 81% of respondents preferred cash to be directed toward commercializing technology rather than returned to investors. Investment returns and capital growth were the leading reasons for holding the shares, while 63% wanted Nanoco to remain listed.

Image Sensing Is the Main Priority

Nanoco identified quantum-dot-enabled image sensing as its priority market, bringing together its intellectual property, experience, customer relationships and commercial opportunity. Its four quantum-dot material sets cover wavelengths from near-infrared at 800 nanometers to mid-wave infrared at about 3,500 nanometers.

Heavy-Metal-Free Technology Offers Differentiation

The company presented itself as a pioneer in heavy-metal-free quantum dots, supported by a deep patent portfolio, technical know-how and paid development partnerships. Its materials are designed to be deposited directly onto standard CMOS chips, with potential volume sensor costs ranging from €10 to €100.

Wide Range of Sensor Applications

Management sees potential for short-wave infrared sensors in automotive systems, defense, security, LiDAR, robotics and under-display sensing. Other possible uses include material sorting, motion detection, wafer inspection and wider industrial applications.

Large Market Opportunity, But Timing Has Shifted

Nanoco cited a Yole Intelligence forecast for the short-wave infrared imaging market to grow from $322 million in 2022 to $2.9 billion by 2028. Management said the forecast is now dated and that reaching that scale around 2031 may be a more realistic assumption, although defense demand is already supporting growth.

Customer Pipeline Is Expanding

The company reported good global coverage of image-sensor opportunities and a pipeline of Asian customers targeting high-volume markets. It is also working with new FY2027 customers on potential quantum-dot applications, while selectively pursuing biomedical, photovoltaic, anti-counterfeiting, quantum and niche display opportunities.

Scale-Up Capability Remains In-House

Despite years of headcount reductions, Nanoco said it has retained the facilities and expertise needed for internal scale-up. Management pointed to previous experience scaling and validating first-generation materials with a European customer as evidence of that capability.

Potential Route to Breakeven

Management outlined a potential path to cash flow breakeven at roughly £5 million of revenue in about two years. The proposed progression runs from current contract revenue of £600,000 to £1 million, £2 million and £4 million, without a significant expansion of the cost base.

AI Exploration Begins in Research

Nanoco’s finance department is already using artificial intelligence extensively, while researchers are discussing how it could shorten the feedback loop in development work. The company is still assessing practical uses rather than presenting AI as a material near-term earnings driver.

Cash Balance Falls

Cash ended FY2026 at £9.3 million, down from £14.0 million a year earlier. The £4.7 million decline reflects continued cash burn and underlines the importance of converting development programs into commercial revenue.

Litigation and Review Costs Weighed on Results

Items below EBITDA totaled £4.3 million, including £3.7 million of litigation costs, £0.5 million for the strategic review and £0.1 million of restructuring. Litigation linked to LG cost about £0.3 million, while the Shoei proceedings generated significant discovery expenses.

Higher Depreciation Included an Impairment

Depreciation and amortization increased to £2.0 million from the prior year. The rise was largely caused by a one-off impairment of right-of-use assets with one year remaining on their associated lease term.

No New Display Licensing Deals Identified

Nanoco said it currently sees no further reasonable opportunities to claim damages from other potential display infringers, though it will continue monitoring the market. Management also does not presently see a large licensing opportunity in display technology.

Delisting Proposal Withdrawn

Indicative voting and relatively low turnout suggested that a proposed delisting resolution was unlikely to pass. The meeting was adjourned indefinitely and the resolution was withdrawn after the Board concluded that shareholders wanted Nanoco to remain listed.

Strategy Communication Needs Improvement

The shareholder consultation found that 42% of respondents did not clearly understand Nanoco’s strategy. Only 39% had watched the previous Investor Meet Company presentation, highlighting the challenge of improving engagement through webinars and live question-and-answer sessions.

Adoption and Timing Are Major Risks

Management identified customer delay or nonadoption as the company’s key business risk, a concern also cited by 70% of shareholder respondents. Commercialization involves complex devices and long supply chains, while adoption and timing are largely controlled by customers rather than Nanoco.

Customer Concentration Remains a Concern

Nanoco acknowledged significant customer concentration risk, noting that it has previously suffered from relying too heavily on one relationship. The company is seeking new leads and more customers to create a broader and more resilient revenue base.

Performance Gap Versus InGaAs

Current quantum-dot sensors deliver about 30% quantum efficiency, with some results approaching 70%, compared with 80% to 90% for established InGaAs technology. Management cautioned that comparisons can vary with voltage and temperature, but performance remains an important commercialization hurdle.

Scale-Up Timing Remains Uncertain

Management could not give a firm timetable for when the major Asian customer would move beyond scale-up, saying the process takes as long as it takes. Demand at the time of the presentation was broadly in line with the prior year, although an increase was expected over the following six months and beyond.

Forward Guidance Points to Gradual Growth

Nanoco’s FY2027 opening order book is £6.2 million, while monthly gross cash costs are expected to remain near £0.3 million to £0.4 million and planned device and IP investment totals about £0.2 million. Management expects Asian material demand to rise as the first customer approaches production, with cash flow breakeven targeted at about £5 million of revenue in roughly two years.

Nanoco’s call combined improved finances and a stronger commercial platform with a clear warning that meaningful adoption may take time. Investors have a leaner business, substantial order-book support and a potential breakeven route to watch, but must weigh those positives against cash burn, execution risk and the gap between promising technology and volume sales.

Gold Production Target Remains Intact

McEwen Mining said it remains on track to double gold production by 2030. The company is targeting annual output of 250,000 to 300,000 ounces, despite the execution challenges exposed during the third quarter.

Gold Bar Returns to Positive Cash Flow

Gold Bar recorded its highest monthly production in 15 months during October and returned to positive cash flow. Management expects output of about 3,000 gold equivalent ounces per month through November and December, with early budgeting pointing to a similar monthly average in 2027.

Fox Complex Costs Improve

Costs at the Fox Complex returned within guidance in October after elevated third-quarter all-in sustaining costs. Management expects costs to remain within guidance and decline as operations shift toward the Stock Mine.

Stock Mine Could Lift Profitability

Stock is entering its ore zone and is expected to outperform Froome, helped by higher recoveries, no royalty, no haulage to the mill and roughly 30% more milling capacity from softer rock. The benefits are expected to begin in December and strengthen in early 2027.

Portfolio Moves Toward Longer-Life Mines

The company is transitioning from shorter-life operations to a longer-life portfolio. Stock is expected to operate for 8.5 to 9 years, Grey Fox for about 15 years, while Gold Bar could expand from a three- to four-year mine life to more than a decade with Trinity, Windfall and Lookout; the Mexico mill could run for 10 to 20 years, depending on permits.

Los Azules Engineering Advances

Engineering cost estimates and the execution plan for Los Azules remain on track for completion around year-end. Metso has begun work on major process plant packages, four international firms bid for the EPCM contract and bid evaluation is expected before year-end, with a final investment decision and full financing targeted for mid-2027.

Feasibility Study Offers Potential Upside

An updated Los Azules feasibility study is targeted for February 2027. It will incorporate better-than-expected geotechnical results, a higher long-term copper price based on analyst consensus and current costs from recent bids, while management sees potential for more copper and a longer mine life.

Permitting Reaches Key Milestones

Los Azules received approval to connect to Argentina’s national grid, permits for its 3,000-bed construction camp and Candadito camp, and approval to explore the neighboring Marisa I property. Basic engineering for the power line and substation is complete and ready for tender, leaving the water concession as the main outstanding permit.

Liquidity Supports Los Azules Work

Commitments under McEwen Copper’s term loan facility rose to $240 million in August. At quarter-end, McEwen Copper held $157.8 million in cash and equivalents and $138.9 million in working capital, while McEwen Mining had $49 million in cash and $10 million in marketable securities, followed by $55 million raised from selling noncore profits in October.

Resource Base Provides Scale

McEwen reported 5.8 million ounces of gold resources across all categories. Management described Los Azules as equivalent to a 56 million-ounce gold deposit on a gold-equivalent basis, with attractive costs and additional technical work expected to produce results in early 2027.

Safety and Community Support Remain Strong

Los Azules completed the third quarter without a reportable incident or lost-time injury. A survey of 2,529 residents in 10 nearby communities found that 97% accepted the project and 90% trusted it, while local suppliers received $27.7 million in business from 2023 through mid-2026.

San Jose Recovery Expected

Management expects San Jose to recover much of its lost production in the fourth quarter and meet its annual guidance. A return to clay material should improve grades, while recoveries are expected to return to first- and second-quarter levels after the operation recently achieved strong throughput following its mill expansion.

El Gallo Mill Construction Starts

Earthworks have begun for the El Gallo mill, marking the start of construction activity. Spending is expected to be modest in the fourth quarter and become more consistent in the first half of 2027 after EPCM contracts are finalized, with costs capitalized as the project advances.

Management Labels Quarter Unacceptable

Management openly described the third quarter as very difficult and unacceptable. It emphasized that McEwen, as a mining and gold company, must generate profits, but did not do so during the period.

Gold Bar Faced Management Problems

Gold Bar’s problems began in the second quarter and continued into the third, including weak oversight, insufficient detail and delayed decisions. Personnel changes have been made, although management said a heap-leach operation needs time before those changes translate into higher output.

Fox AISC Was Distorted by Development Costs

Fox Complex AISC rose because development costs for incremental ore were concentrated in the third quarter rather than spread across the remaining six to nine months of mining. Feeding the mill from a low-grade stockpile, due to excess capacity, also pushed costs higher.

Snowfall Hurt San Jose Output

Record snowfall in Argentina and Chile increased moisture at the San Jose mill and created plant problems. The operation used lower-grade, sulfide-rich stockpiles, reducing gold and silver recoveries while lowering production and increasing costs.

Los Azules Access Delay Raises Schedule Risk

The Andes experienced its heaviest snowfall in more than two decades, delaying the reopening of the Los Azules access road. Road crews expect to reach the site in early 2027, although snowmelt and spring weather could delay that further and push site work behind schedule.

First Copper Target Has Several Conditions

Los Azules continues to target first copper in 2030, but management stressed that the date depends on site access, the selected recovery measures, completion of investment decision work, project financing and customary approvals. The statement highlights the execution risk surrounding the development timetable.

Construction Financing Remains Uncommitted

Potential construction funding sources include senior project debt, strategic-investor equity at the McEwen Copper level and a possible initial public offering of McEwen Copper. Management emphasized that none of these financing sources is committed at present.

Future Equity Could Dilute Ownership

Any new equity would be raised at the McEwen Copper level. If McEwen Mining does not participate, its current 46.3% ownership stake would decline, although the size of any reduction depends on the eventual debt level and equity price.

Diesel Costs Lifted Gold Bar Expenses

Higher diesel prices increased Gold Bar’s third-quarter cash costs by approximately $200 per ounce. Management said the effect at other operations was $50 per ounce or less and was not material.

San Jose Dividends Pause in 2026

McEwen does not expect further San Jose dividends during the rest of 2026. Closure obligations are substantially or fully met, however, and additional dividends are expected in 2027 unless significant capital development follows a discovery.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management reaffirmed its goal of 250,000 to 300,000 ounces of gold production by 2030, with Gold Bar expected to sustain October-like output and Fox costs moving lower. Los Azules remains targeted for first copper in 2030, a feasibility study in February 2027 and fully financed FID in mid-2027, while San Jose is expected to deliver a strong fourth quarter and El Gallo spending should increase in the first half of 2027.

data.title: Rogers Sugar Earnings Call Signals Stronger Business Ahead
data.description:
Rogers Sugar ((TSE:RSI)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Rogers Sugar’s earnings call carried a strongly positive tone, led by record adjusted EBITDA, five straight years of growth, improved Sugar margins and a record Maple quarter. Management also highlighted labor certainty, solid liquidity and progress on LEAP, while acknowledging softer revenue, lower Sugar volumes, trade uncertainty and higher project spending ahead.

Record Full-Year Profitability

Rogers Sugar reported record consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $160 million in 2026, up from $150 million in 2025. Adjusted net earnings rose to $74 million, or about $0.58 per share, from $72 million, or $0.57 per share.

Five Years of EBITDA Growth

Adjusted EBITDA has increased from $91 million in 2021 to $160 million in 2026, a 76% improvement. Management said the company exceeded its internal targets and is fundamentally stronger than it was five years ago.

Labor Certainty Across the Network

The company secured a five-year labor agreement at its Montreal facility through May 2031. Agreements at Taber and Granby were also extended, giving Rogers labor certainty across its production network through the LEAP commissioning period and beyond.

Sugar Margins Expand

Sugar adjusted gross margin increased to $256 per metric ton in 2026 from $224 in 2025. Management credited the Rogers Refined operating framework, customer and product mix, and disciplined cost control.

Sugar Volume Beats Recent Guidance

Full-year Sugar volume fell 29,000 metric tons to 753,000 metric tons, but exceeded the latest guidance by 10,000 metric tons. Opportunistic fourth-quarter exports helped offset the decline, while the domestic franchise remained stable.

Record Fourth Quarter for Maple

Maple volume rose by 2 million pounds to 56 million pounds for the year, supported by existing customers. Fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA reached almost $8 million, up $3 million year over year and marking a record quarter for the segment.

Maple Margins Improve

Maple fourth-quarter adjusted gross margin improved to 13% from 9% a year earlier. Full-year margin rose to 10.8% from 10.4%, reflecting better segment performance.

Maple Demand Gains Momentum

Management reported stronger demand from existing customers, favorable market conditions and growing global interest in Maple. Early 2027 bookings were described as strong and consistent with the momentum seen late in 2026.

Maple Supply Secured

Rogers has secured enough Maple supply to meet customer commitments through the first half of 2027. The company expects to use the 2027 crop for the second half and said its supplier relationships and purchasing infrastructure should prevent disruption.

LEAP Remains on Schedule

The redesigned Toronto logistics infrastructure is expected to deliver the same operating outcome at a lower cost, with savings redirected to the Montreal refinery. Total LEAP spending is still expected to remain within the $300 million ceiling, with commissioning targeted for June 2027.

LEAP Construction Progress

Rogers said higher civil infrastructure costs were offset by savings elsewhere within the existing budget. Construction is expected to be largely complete in the spring, some areas are already being commissioned, and management reported no significant risk to the June 2027 start date.

Balance Sheet Remains Sound

Rogers had drawn $100 million on its revolving credit facility at the end of the fourth quarter. That was $16 million below the third quarter and $47 million below year-end 2025, while the company remained in full compliance with its financial covenants.

Cash Flow Supports LEAP

Higher adjusted EBITDA over the past three years has lifted operating cash flow. This allowed Rogers to fund more of LEAP, reduce its revolving-credit draw and lower borrowing costs.

Underlying Free Cash Flow Holds Up

Free cash flow was $78 million in 2026, down $25 million from the prior year. Management said that excluding a $15 million tax payment related to 2025, paid early in 2026, free cash flow would have increased by $5 million.

Dividend Continuity

The Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.09 per common share, payable on or before January 20, 2027. Rogers has maintained an uninterrupted quarterly dividend for more than 16 years.

2027 Sugar Volume Outlook

Rogers expects 2027 Sugar volume to range from 730,000 to 750,000 metric tons. Management described domestic demand and customer relationships as stable, with the range broadly consistent with 2026 after considering the prior year’s extra week.

2027 Maple Volume Outlook

Maple volume is expected to remain aligned with 2026 levels. Management said the global demand environment is stable and that the business is entering 2027 with positive momentum.

Capital Spending to Normalize

Total 2027 capital spending is expected to be slightly below $100 million. The plan includes about $25 million for Sugar projects, $70 million for LEAP and $1 million to $2 million for Maple automation, with spending expected to normalize in 2028 and beyond.

Revenue Declines on Lower Sugar Prices

Revenue fell to $1.2 billion in 2026 from $1.3 billion in 2025, mainly because average raw No. 11 sugar prices were lower. Management said hedging limited the effect of those price changes on profitability.

Sugar Volume Faces Trade Pressure

Sugar volume declined by 29,000 metric tons during the year. Rogers also expects lower-margin exports to decrease in 2027 because of current trade policies between Canada and the United States.

Fourth-Quarter Sugar EBITDA Falls

Sugar fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA declined $3 million to $32 million. Higher production costs outweighed benefits from stronger industrial and export sales, lower raw sugar procurement costs and a favorable product mix.

Sugar Offsets Cost and Volume Challenges

Full-year Sugar adjusted EBITDA increased $9 million to $138 million. The gain was partly reduced by higher manufacturing costs, nonrecurring pension costs, weaker export volume linked to U.S. trade conditions and lower liquid sugar sales.

Fourth-Quarter Earnings Decline

Fourth-quarter adjusted net earnings were $14 million, or about $0.11 per share, with adjusted earnings per share down $0.05 year over year. The decline included a nonrecurring $4.8 million impairment charge tied to the LEAP logistics redesign.

Montreal Refinery Costs Rise

The final Montreal refinery phase is costing more than expected because of the complexity of civil work in the existing building. Rogers recorded a $4.8 million impairment for engineering and other capitalized costs made unnecessary by the logistics redesign.

Leverage Expected to Rise

Leverage is expected to increase during the final LEAP phase as Rogers spends about $70 million on the project in 2027. Management plans to reduce total debt relative to adjusted EBITDA over the medium term.

Sugar Pricing Faces Competition

Management expects slight downward pressure on Sugar pricing because of current market dynamics and competition. After several years of margin gains, Sugar margins are expected to level out in 2027 and remain broadly similar to 2026 after excluding nonrecurring items.

Trade Policy Creates Risks

Targeted product bans affecting certain product codes could hurt some industrial customers, including products that comply with CUSMA. If the measures persist, Rogers said some parts of its order book could experience volume erosion.

Export Planning Remains Difficult

Opportunistic exports helped the fourth quarter, but management does not expect all those sales to continue in 2027. The changing trade environment makes export volumes difficult to forecast.

Maple Experiences Uneven Performance

The second and third quarters were challenging for Maple, and Rogers lost several European accounts. Management described that market as highly competitive and lower margin, prompting a renewed focus on more profitable opportunities.

Maple Pricing Negotiations Continue

Negotiations between CIE and PPAQ over pricing and buying conditions for the 2027 Maple crop remain underway. Rogers expects inflationary pricing and some pressure on margins, but said it expects to pass commodity cost increases on to customers.

LEAP Drives 2027 Spending

About $70 million of 2027 capital spending is earmarked for LEAP completion. The amount is included in total annual capital spending expected to be slightly below $100 million.

Consumer Pressures Closely Watched

Management cited food and cocoa inflation, weaker consumer purchasing power and the possible effect of GLP-1 drugs on some markets. Rogers has not yet seen a material impact from GLP-1 treatments on its business.

2027 Guidance and LEAP Outlook

Rogers expects Sugar volume of 730,000 to 750,000 metric tons, stable Maple volume and Sugar margins broadly similar to 2026 after excluding $15 million to $18 million of nonrecurring items. LEAP remains targeted for June 2027 commissioning, with greater benefits expected in 2028 and capital spending set to normalize thereafter.

Overall, Rogers Sugar enters the next phase with record profitability, stronger margins, secured labor agreements and improving Maple demand. Trade uncertainty, softer exports, cost pressure and higher leverage remain risks, but management’s confidence in the business and its medium-term prospects was clear.

Women’s, men’s and kids divisions all delivered double-digit growth, with kids and baby leading the group. Management pointed to stronger seasonal assortments, improved fabrics, wider product ranges, better launch timing and more effective product storytelling.

Gap Expanded Customer Engagement

Gap added 430,000 followers during the year, taking its membership base to 35 million and generating 45 million online engagements. Several campaigns ranked first on Weibo’s star product influence list during their launch periods, highlighting stronger brand visibility.

Gap Accelerated Store Expansion

Hunter expanded its range through collaborations with TAGI and GANNI and introduced a lightweight summer outdoor collection. It entered Shenzhen, opened its first Thailand flagship at Bangkok’s ICONSIAM and ended the quarter with 28 stores.

An AI pilot that began in Gap’s e-commerce operations has become a group-wide productivity program with a 15-month roadmap, milestones and cost targets. Applications include product listings, campaign planning, virtual design and data processing.

Management expects the AI roadmap to reduce store-operation labor costs by 25% to 30% by the end of 2027. The Gap pilot has already improved productivity at the individual-unit level, according to the company.

Baozun lifted its group-level 2028 non-GAAP operating profit target to CNY 700 million. Management said AI deployment and lean transformation should support changes in BEC’s margin structure during 2026 and 2027.

The third version of AI Dianxiaomi is being piloted with Baozun’s brand partners to improve online explanations of product information and promotional mechanisms. With about 500 partners, the company said deeper customization is needed for inventory, content creation and other complex omnichannel tasks.

Working Capital and Fulfillment Improved

Working-capital turnover improved to 123 days from 183 days a year earlier, while inventory turnover shortened to 126 days from 180 days. Fulfillment costs fell 9% to CNY 453 million, reflecting ongoing cost-optimization work.

Emerging Brands Remain a Strategic Focus

Baozun continues investing in emerging brands through positioning, category expansion, retail growth and balanced online-first development. Management said Gap’s established teams, systems and infrastructure could help newer brands absorb costs and shorten their ramp-up periods.

Quarterly Operating Loss Increased

Third-quarter non-GAAP operating loss widened to CNY 41 million from CNY 11 million a year earlier. Management attributed the result mainly to BEC seasonality and planned investment in emerging BBM brands.

BEC Services Revenue Was Flat

BEC services revenue remained unchanged at CNY 1.4 billion in the quarter despite overall BEC growth. The result shows that product sales, rather than core services, were the main source of momentum during the period.

E-Commerce Product Margins Declined

E-commerce product-sales gross margin fell to 12.1% from 13.1% a year earlier. Management linked the decline to category-mix changes while it reshaped the product-sales portfolio and prioritized earnings quality.

Sales and Marketing Costs Increased

Sales and marketing expenses rose by CNY 147 million to CNY 1 billion. BEC spending increased by CNY 98 million, mainly for creative content and campaigns on Douyin and RedNote, while BBM spending rose CNY 51 million because of store expansion and marketing.

Seasonality Weighed on the Third Quarter

Management described the third quarter as e-commerce’s lightest seasonal period, with the effect amplified because partners completed a large share of annual plans in the first half. BEC also faced weaker consumption sentiment during the quarter.

Young Brands Still Require Investment

Hunter, Sweaty Betty and other newer brands remain in an investment and expansion phase. Baozun is balancing store-opening costs and marketing spending, while retaining the flexibility to invest more when faster scaling opportunities emerge.

Guidance Points to a Stronger Growth Phase

Baozun expects Gap to reach CNY 2 billion in revenue and full-year breakeven in 2026, while opening more than 50 stores, including about 20 in the fourth quarter. For 2027, it is targeting 40 to 50 additional stores and continued double-digit sales growth, alongside a strong fourth-quarter finish.

Longer-Term Targets Rely on AI and Margin Gains

The company expects its AI roadmap to cut store-operation labor costs by 25% to 30% by the end of 2027. Management also expects BEC’s margin structure to begin transforming in 2026 and 2027, while reaffirming the three-year plan behind the raised CNY 700 million 2028 non-GAAP operating profit target.

Baozun’s call combined solid growth with a clearer path toward better profitability, led by Gap, BEC and efficiency programs. The higher profit target and AI ambitions strengthen the investment story, but investors will still watch quarterly losses, margin pressure and the cost of expanding newer brands.

Average daily international room nights sold climbed more than 40% year over year to another record. International accommodation revenue now represents 5% of total accommodation reservation revenue, up from 3% last year.

International Air Ticketing Gains Momentum

Average daily international air ticket volume reached a record after rising more than 16% year over year. International air ticketing revenue accounted for 9.6% of transportation ticketing revenue, nearly four percentage points higher than a year earlier.

Hotel Management Network Expands Rapidly

Tongcheng’s hotel network approached 3,800 properties at the end of September, nearly 700 more than at the start of the year. Wanda Hotels and Resorts operated more than 330 hotels, resorts and commercial complexes, while Elong Hotel Technology managed nearly 3,500 hotels.

Hotel Management Becomes a Growth Engine

Hotel management revenue more than doubled and contributed over 40% of other revenue in the quarter. Elong Hotel Technology’s focus on mid-scale and upper mid-scale brands supported year-over-year growth in both average daily rate and revenue per available room.

International Hotel Supply Broadens

The company continued to add hotel supply and products across Southeast Asia and Northeast Asia. Wanda Hotels and Resorts also entered Africa for the first time this year, extending the group’s international reach.

Other Business Revenue Advances

Other business revenue grew 36.1% year over year to RMB 1.1 billion. The increase was mainly driven by the stronger performance of the hotel management business.

User Engagement and Monetization Strengthen

Standalone app daily active users exceeded 5.6 million ahead of the National Day holiday, setting a new record. Twelve-month average revenue per user surpassed RMB 82, an increase of nearly 11% year over year.

Large User Base Supports Scale

Tongcheng served more than 2 billion cumulative travelers during the 12 months ended September. Average paying users reached 250 million, implying that users made more than eight purchases on average during the period.

AI Adoption Gains Traction

DeepTrip had served nearly 20 million users since launch, with related order volumes continuing to grow. Tongcheng is integrating AI across trip planning, product discovery, bookings, customer service and internal operations.

AI Improves Service and Efficiency

AI-powered presale consultation for packaged tours improved efficiency and significantly raised order conversion. Flight assistants helped users search by budget and schedule, while AI customer-service tools identified pain points, improved issue resolution and reduced handling time.

Weixin AI Assistant Enters Testing

Tongcheng completed its initial integration with the Weixin AI Assistant and entered gray testing. The process is testing user-intent understanding, content retrieval and the complete booking process.

Liquidity Remains Strong

Cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaled RMB 15.7 billion as of September 30, 2026. The balance gives Tongcheng financial flexibility as it invests in growth, pursues strategic opportunities and manages market volatility.

Investigation Has Not Disrupted Operations

Management said it is fully cooperating with an ongoing regulatory investigation involving the company and several OTA platforms. It added that daily business operations remained normal, with no material disruption observed.

Shareholder Returns Under Review

Management said it aims to further enhance shareholder returns this year, subject to board approval. It also emphasized a balanced approach covering business investment, strategic mergers and acquisitions, and returns to shareholders.

Travel Market Faces Persistent Headwinds

China’s travel market continued to face pressure from extreme weather, geopolitical uncertainty, cautious consumer spending and unclear fuel costs. Management described overall industry growth as modest and said travel demand remained under pressure.

Transportation Revenue Declines

Transportation ticketing revenue fell 2% year over year to RMB 2.2 billion. Frequent extreme weather weakened demand, while regulatory adjustments also affected the train-ticketing business.

Tourism Revenue Comes Under Pressure

Tourism revenue declined 6% to RMB 845.9 million. Outbound packaged tours remained affected by geopolitical uncertainty and rising fuel costs, which weighed on consumer demand.

Train Ticketing Faces Regulatory Pressure

Management expects train-ticketing regulation to continue affecting revenue and profitability. The segment’s contribution to OTA revenue has fallen from about 35% in 2018 to roughly 15% to 16% in the third quarter of 2026.

Higher Fuel Costs Weigh on Demand

Aviation fuel surcharges were raised twice in October and November, reaching RMB 80 for domestic routes of 800 kilometers or less and RMB 140 for longer routes. Management said the increases put further pressure on fares, air-ticketing demand and outbound travel.

APU Falls for the First Time

Average paying users declined for the first time in the third quarter. Softer travel demand, higher fuel surcharges, extreme weather and lower train-ticketing volumes all weighed on travel frequency and the paying-user base.

Operating and Marketing Costs Rise

Service development and administrative expenses increased 11% year over year as new businesses added headcount. Excluding share-based compensation, these costs rose to 15% of revenue from 13.8%, while selling and marketing expenses climbed 12.7% and reached 33.3% of revenue.

Transportation Take Rates Face Pressure

Management expects domestic air-ticketing take rates to decline slightly as higher fares reduce demand for value-added services. Train-ticketing volume and take rates are also expected to weaken because of changes in the operating environment.

Other Business Growth May Moderate

Other business revenue growth is expected to slow after three strong quarters, partly because the comparison base now includes Wanda Hotels and Resorts. Advertising growth may also moderate as market conditions soften.

Domestic OTA Competition Intensifies

Management acknowledged a changing competitive landscape, with more internet platforms using existing user traffic and content capabilities to enter travel services. Accommodation is a particular focus of this expanding competition.

Regulatory Review Remains Ongoing

The investigation involving several OTA platforms, including Tongcheng, is continuing. Management declined to discuss specific details but said it would keep reviewing platform policies, business practices and internal compliance measures.

Fourth-Quarter Outlook

Accommodation performance is expected to remain broadly in line with the third quarter, supported by room nights and average daily rates, while its take rate should remain stable. International air ticketing is expected to deliver strong volume and revenue growth, but train ticketing is likely to decline and other business growth should moderate.

Longer-Term Growth Priorities

Management expects hotel management to maintain strong revenue growth and improve profitability, while outbound products could represent about 9% of accommodation and transportation by the end of 2026. It said visibility into the 2027 operating environment remains limited.

Tongcheng Travel’s earnings call showed a company still delivering growth through core OTA services, international travel, hotel management and AI. However, weaker domestic transportation demand, regulation, rising costs and competition could limit near-term momentum, making execution and disciplined investment central to the stock’s outlook.

data.title: Deere Earnings Call Highlights Growth Amid 2027 Risks
data.description:
Deere & Company ((DE)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Deere & Company’s fiscal 2026 earnings call carried a broadly positive tone, supported by strong full-year profitability, disciplined inventories, growth in Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry, and rising technology adoption. However, weak Large Ag conditions, soft overseas markets, tariffs, cost pressures and potential labor disruption kept management’s outlook measured.

Strong Fiscal 2026 Profitability

Deere reported fiscal 2026 net sales and revenues of $47.7 billion, up 4%, while Equipment Operations sales rose 6% to $41.3 billion. Net income attributable to Deere reached $4.86 billion, or $17.95 per diluted share, and the full-year Equipment Operations margin was 12.2%.

Fourth-Quarter Execution

The company ended the year with a 9.3% Equipment Operations margin and fourth-quarter net income of $1.05 billion, or $3.89 per diluted share. All operating segments were in line with or ahead of the guidance issued in the previous quarter.

Structural Margin Improvement

Equipment Operations produced margins above 12% even though Production & Precision Ag remained below trough-cycle levels. Deere said its comparable margin profile was more than 400 basis points higher than in 2016, reflecting better cost control, tighter inventories and a larger technology mix.

Small Ag & Turf Growth

Small Ag & Turf fourth-quarter sales increased 10% to $2.7 billion, driven by higher shipments and favorable pricing, while full-year sales rose about 15%. The segment posted a 15.1% operating margin, and its tractor business in India recorded a fiscal-year sales record.

Construction & Forestry Expansion

Construction & Forestry fourth-quarter sales rose 12% to $3.8 billion, helped by higher volumes and pricing, while full-year sales climbed nearly 22%. Infrastructure, non-residential construction, rental fleet replacement and rental fleet growth supported results that slightly exceeded the company’s annual outlook.

Inventory Discipline

New North American Large Ag equipment inventories remained tight, falling 10% from already low year-earlier levels. Used high-horsepower tractor inventories were down 25% from their peak, used combines declined about 30%, and model-year 2023 and 2024 tractor inventories fell more than 40% year over year.

Large Ag Demand Indicators Improve

North American Early Order Programs were running up double digits, with especially strong planter demand and combine orders also up double digits. Large-tractor backlog momentum improved steadily, with orders in hand extending through the middle of the second quarter.

Precision Ag Adoption Accelerates

Engaged Acres surpassed 530 million globally, Highly Engaged Acres exceeded 200 million, and monthly active digital users grew nearly 25% to more than 500,000. Connected equipment topped 1.2 million machines, while See & Spray covered about 12 million acres and generated average herbicide savings above 50%.

Customer Productivity Gains

See & Spray utilization in the U.S. and Canada increased about 30%, and roughly one-third of recent sprayer orders included the technology. Harvest Settings Automation was used across 11 million combine acres, while Predictive Ground Speed Automation delivered about 20% greater productivity with lower fuel use.

Construction Technology Growth

Sales of grade management, job-site safety and automation solutions grew about 30% in 2026. More than 90% of orders for Deere’s new 20-metric-ton excavators included grade control, while fleet-management solutions were tracking ahead of expectations.

JD AI Assistant Launch

Deere introduced JD, an artificial-intelligence assistant that uses customer operations data to support equipment users. During its first week of full availability, more than 6,000 users in 76 countries held over 10,000 conversations with the service.

Investment in Future Growth

Deere is continuing to invest in customer solutions, factory automation, efficient production and digital platforms. Planned initiatives include Small Ag & Turf applications, excavator development, the Tenna construction platform, Orchard AI and other targeted acquisitions.

Cash Generation and Shareholder Returns

Management projected fiscal 2027 net operating cash flow of $4.5 billion to $5.5 billion. Deere said its priorities remain preserving an A credit rating, funding growth and returning excess cash through dividends and share repurchases.

Cost Control and Pricing

The company reported productivity gains across operations and supplies and said pricing actions are designed to offset expected inflation. Deere is also working with suppliers on sourcing and design changes intended to reduce costs without compromising product quality.

Brazil Technology Opportunity

Brazilian customers ordered factory-installed See & Spray for the first time, with initial adoption running at roughly twice North America’s first-year rate. Deere is also installing JDLink Boost on every Large Ag machine leaving its factories, supporting longer-term digital adoption.

Fourth-Quarter Consolidated Declines

Despite solid full-year performance, fourth-quarter net sales and revenues fell 2% to $12.1 billion, while Equipment Operations sales declined 1% to $10.5 billion. Net income attributable to Deere decreased 1% to $1.05 billion.

Production & Precision Ag Weakness

Production & Precision Ag fourth-quarter sales dropped 15% to $4 billion, mainly because of lower shipments, while operating profit fell to $406 million. Full-year sales declined about 9% across North America, South America and Europe, although lower production costs and currency effects provided some offset.

Tight Farm Economics

Large Ag customers continue to face narrow farm margins, high input costs and volatile commodity markets. Deere said crop prices have retreated from recent highs, conditions that are likely to slow the pace of industry recovery.

Regional Agriculture Challenges

Europe faces pressure from weaker crop yields, elevated input costs and tighter lending conditions, while South America remains constrained by high interest rates, currency volatility and uncertain weather. These factors are delaying purchases and keeping regional equipment volumes near historically low levels.

Small Ag & Turf Market Constraints

Small Ag & Turf industry sales in the U.S. and Canada are expected to remain roughly flat as high mortgage rates and a soft housing market limit turf-equipment demand. Europe is also facing some downward market pressure.

Construction Margin Pressure

Construction & Forestry’s fourth-quarter operating profit slipped slightly to $339 million, producing an 8.9% margin. Higher production, selling, administrative and research costs outweighed favorable pricing, while weak residential construction, forestry markets and possible data-center spending risks remain concerns.

Financial Services Decline

Worldwide Financial Services fourth-quarter net income fell to $231 million. The decline reflected weaker financing spreads, a smaller average portfolio and a higher provision for credit losses.

Fiscal 2027 Profit Range

Deere expects fiscal 2027 net income of $4.5 billion to $5.25 billion, a range below or near the prior year’s result. The forecast includes about $500 million of higher pension-related impacts, including a potential one-time, tax-adjusted non-cash settlement charge of $250 million to $400 million.

Tariff Headwinds

Direct tariff costs exceeded $1.1 billion in 2026 before refunds, and Deere expects the 2027 run rate to ease slightly to about $1 billion. Because last year’s refunds will not repeat, the company anticipates a roughly $300 million net headwind.

Raw Material and Freight Costs

Steel, other raw materials and freight remain on an upward trend. Deere said these costs are incorporated into its outlook and should be addressed through pricing actions and procurement efforts.

UAW Contract Risk

Deere’s labor agreements with the UAW expire at the end of fiscal 2027, and the company is preparing for several possible outcomes, including a work stoppage. Such actions could create a notable increase in working capital needs, particularly in the fourth quarter.

2027 Margin Investment

Growth investments, tariffs and other pressures are expected to weigh on Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry margins in 2027. At the midpoint, Small Ag & Turf’s margin is about two points lower, with roughly half the reduction tied to tariffs and half to investment.

Soft Forestry and Housing Markets

Global forestry markets are expected to remain roughly flat as weak housing activity limits improvement. Elevated mortgage rates continue to weigh on residential construction and smaller and mid-sized contractors.

Fiscal 2027 Guidance

Deere expects Production & Precision Ag sales to rise 5% to 15%, with a 12.5% to 14.5% margin, while Small Ag & Turf sales should be roughly flat with a 12.5% to 13.5% margin. Construction & Forestry sales are forecast to range from flat to up 10%, with a 9.5% to 11.5% margin, and Financial Services income is expected to reach $900 million.

The company also projects a 23% to 25% effective tax rate, net income of $4.5 billion to $5.25 billion and operating cash flow of $4.5 billion to $5.5 billion. Management expects pricing, procurement and productivity actions to help offset tariffs, inflation and currency pressure, but pension costs and labor uncertainty remain important risks.

Deere’s call showed a business with stronger structural margins, healthy technology adoption and encouraging order signals in North American Large Ag and construction. Still, subdued farm economics, regional weakness and several cost and execution risks suggest that fiscal 2027 will be a year of measured recovery rather than a broad-based rebound.

data.title: GDS Holdings Earnings Call Signals AI-Driven Growth
data.description:
GDS Holdings ((GDS)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

GDS Holdings delivered a predominantly positive message on its earnings call, pointing to strong AI infrastructure demand, solid bookings and high-quality customers in China. Management also highlighted stable data-center economics, improving utilization and clear visibility into future billings and EBITDA, while acknowledging near-term utilization pressure, legacy contract repricing and higher planned net debt.

AI Demand Drives China Focus

GDS said it remains fully focused on providing data-center services in China, where artificial intelligence is developing rapidly. Management described demand for AI infrastructure as robust, supporting the company’s growth plans.

Bookings Maintain Strong Momentum

Bookings reached 686 megawatts in the first nine months of 2026. GDS expects to reach its full-year target of about 1 gigawatt, while its backlog model uses an assumption of 950 megawatts in new bookings.

Leading Internet Customers Anchor Growth

More than 80% of new business is coming from China’s three largest Internet and cloud customers. GDS described these clients as high quality and noted that it has served them for many years.

Selective, Contracted Expansion

GDS said it remains selective when adding new business and favors orders based on domestic technologies. Take-or-pay contracts, with customer move-in periods averaging 12 months, provide support for the disclosed bookings.

Projects Have Strong Delivery Support

New projects are located in national hubs with available land and power, backed by local and central government support. Management said approvals are based on proven demand and financing capacity, while supply-chain bottlenecks are not currently an issue.

Data-Center Economics Remain Stable

Management reported stable pricing, development costs and project yields. Current pricing, it said, continues to support reasonable risk-adjusted returns despite a competitive and rapidly changing market.

Bookings Are Fully Funded

GDS said its roughly 1 gigawatt of expected bookings for 2026 is fully funded by existing financial resources. The company also has access to low-cost domestic bank debt and domestic equity markets through its asset-monetization strategy.

Shanghai C-REIT Platform Advances

GDS has established one of only two data-center REITs listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. It is at an advanced stage of seeking approval for its first post-IPO asset injection, which it expects to complete early next year.

Backlog Visibility Continues to Improve

The company began 2026 with a 450-megawatt backlog. Assuming 950 megawatts of new bookings and 250 megawatts of billings during the year, GDS expects its year-end backlog to reach 1.15 gigawatts.

Billings Could Exceed 2.4 Gigawatts

GDS expects total billings to reach 1.4 gigawatts by the end of 2026. After construction and ramp-up, the 1.15-gigawatt backlog is expected to become fully billable within two years, supporting billings above 2.4 gigawatts by the end of 2028, before additional new business.

Contracted EBITDA Points Higher

Annualized adjusted EBITDA is expected to reach about RMB 5.5 billion in the fourth quarter of 2026. After factoring in churn, asset monetization and price resets, GDS projects RMB 6.7 billion in the fourth quarter of 2028, a 21% increase that excludes new business after 2026.

Third-Quarter Growth Remained Positive

On a pro forma basis, third-quarter revenue rose 11.9% year over year, while adjusted EBITDA increased 6.2%. Management said the company remains on track to meet its revised 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA targets.

CapEx Timing Changes, Not Project Plans

GDS reduced full-year CapEx guidance to RMB 8.5 billion from RMB 10 billion because of a small shift in supplier payment timing. CapEx incurred during 2026 is expected to total about RMB 12 billion, with management emphasizing that project execution remains unchanged.

Funding Plan Supports Backlog Delivery

GDS expects to end 2026 with RMB 32 billion of net debt and plans to spend RMB 16 billion over the following two years to complete capacity tied to its year-end backlog. Management said the company is fully funded for delivery and expects net debt of about RMB 38 billion by the end of 2028.

Liquidity and Financing Remain Substantial

Cash resources stood at about RMB 19 billion, while operating cash flow reached RMB 2 billion in the first nine months excluding one-time items. GDS finances new investment with roughly 60% debt and 40% equity, using project loans, cash flow and asset-monetization proceeds.

Utilization Has Room to Recover

Management said utilization is currently at its highest level ever. However, as newly committed capacity enters service, utilization is expected to temporarily fall back into the 70s before recovering and trending toward the mid- to high 80s.

Move-In Assumptions Hold Steady

Customer contracts continue to allow move-in over an average period of 12 months. GDS said there has been no change to its assumptions about customer move-in cadence or the pace of ramp-up.

Domestic Technology Supports Supply Confidence

All current bookings rely on domestic technologies, according to management. GDS said it remains confident that its supply chain has no bottlenecks and that external volatility has not changed its delivery schedule or backlog assumptions.

2026 Revenue and EBITDA Targets Unchanged

GDS maintained its full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance. The decision reflects management’s continued confidence in operating performance despite a temporary utilization dip and slower adjusted EBITDA growth than revenue growth.

Revenue Growth Outpaced EBITDA

The third-quarter figures showed a difference in growth rates, with pro forma revenue up 11.9% and adjusted EBITDA up 6.2% year over year. The gap reflects near-term operating pressures as the company expands capacity and continues to manage pricing changes.

Net Debt Will Rise With Investment

Net debt stood at 5.1 times last-quarter annualized adjusted EBITDA at the end of the third quarter. GDS expects leverage to increase as it funds backlog delivery, rising from RMB 32 billion at the end of 2026 to about RMB 38 billion in 2028.

Legacy Contract Repricing Nears Completion

GDS remains in the final phase of repricing legacy contracts as they renew. Management expects the process to be largely completed within the next 18 months, which should clarify the effect of older agreements on future economics.

Convertible Bond Reserve Set Aside

The company has reserved RMB 4 billion in preparation for the early redemption of a convertible bond next year. The reserve is part of GDS’s broader liquidity and capital-management planning.

Guidance Points to Expanding Backlog and EBITDA

GDS expects about 1 gigawatt of 2026 bookings, a 1.15-gigawatt year-end backlog and 1.4 gigawatts of total billings. It projects billings above 2.4 gigawatts by the end of 2028, annualized adjusted EBITDA of RMB 5.5 billion in the fourth quarter of 2026 and RMB 6.7 billion in the fourth quarter of 2028, while utilization may briefly return to the 70s before reaching the mid- to high 80s.

Overall, GDS presented a confident outlook built on AI demand, contracted growth and a large, increasingly visible backlog. The main risks are the temporary utilization decline, slower EBITDA growth, legacy repricing and higher leverage, but management maintained its 2026 targets and said funding for planned expansion is in place.
